item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E004","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The article reports that the central CCP adopted academic opinions partly because its own information agencies could be slow or affected by conflicts of interest; academics were viewed as relatively distant from agency interests and able to use a wide range of research methods, while career and monetary incentives tied their output more closely to CCP political needs.","notes":["The excerpt does not explicitly characterize academics as more 'analytical and objective' sources."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E007","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"From 2013 onward, the CCP, State Council, and research institutes incorporated consultative information into academics’ evaluations, promotions, research funding, and talent-scheme applications; some institutions offered awards of up to 100,000 yuan for reports receiving Politburo Standing Committee instructions. The article reports that this created career opportunities and tied academics more closely to Party needs, while leaving little room for independent research in politically sensitive areas.","notes":["'Expanded policy access' is too definitive; the excerpt presents empowerment as an argument and says policy influence is difficult to trace."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"On 17 March 2023, a UN special-procedures communication reported information concerning multiple cases filed against Jimmy Lai under various legal provisions, including the National Security Law; the listed mandates included arbitrary detention, freedom of opinion and expression, peaceful assembly and association, and judicial independence.","notes":["The excerpt lists these issues as mandates but does not itself state that each was established as a fact or final finding in Lai’s cases."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0011-E012","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
